classification.difficultyReason: Sketch twelve parabolas using exact intercepts, vertices and symmetry axes, including irrational roots and graphs without real x-intercepts.

content.prompt: Sketch the graph, labelling the vertex, axis of symmetry and the intercepts.

answer.short: Upward-opening parabola. Vertex $(3,-4)$; axis $x=3$; intercepts $(1,0)$, $(5,0)$ and $(0,5)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2-6x+9-9+5\\y&=(x-3)^2-4\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(3,-4)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=3$.
At $x=0$, $y=5$.
$$\begin{align*}(x-1)(x-5)&=0\\x&=1\text{ or }5\end{align*}$$
Plot the intercepts $(0,5)$, $(1,0)$ and $(5,0)$ and the vertex. Draw an upward-opening parabola symmetric about $x=3$.

spec.description: Complete solution graph with vertex, intercepts and dashed symmetry axis; no grid.
spec.mathematics: y=(x-3)^2-4; vertex (3,-4); axis x=3; roots 1,5; y-intercept 5.

answer.short: Downward-opening parabola. Vertex $(-\frac12,\frac{25}{4})$; axis $x=-\frac12$; intercepts $(-3,0)$, $(2,0)$ and $(0,6)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(x^2+x)+6\\y&=-\left(x+\frac12\right)^2+\frac{25}{4}\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-\frac12,\frac{25}{4})$ and the axis is $x=-\frac12$. At $x=0$, $y=6$.
$$\begin{align*}-(x+3)(x-2)&=0\\x&=-3\text{ or }2\end{align*}$$
Plot these features and draw a downward-opening parabola symmetric about $x=-\frac12$.

spec.description: Downward parabola with all intercepts, vertex and symmetry axis.

answer.short: Downward-opening parabola. Vertex and y-intercept $(0,4)$; axis $x=0$; x-intercepts $(-2,0)$ and $(2,0)$.
answer.worked:
The equation is $y=-(x-0)^2+4$, so the vertex is $(0,4)$ and the axis is $x=0$.
$$\begin{align*}4-x^2&=0\\x^2&=4\\x&=\pm2\end{align*}$$
The y-intercept is $(0,4)$. Plot the vertex and x-intercepts and draw a downward-opening parabola symmetric about the y-axis.

spec.description: Symmetry axis coincides with the y-axis, explicitly labelled x=0.

answer.short: Upward-opening parabola. Vertex and x-intercept $(-3,0)$; axis $x=-3$; y-intercept $(0,9)$.
answer.worked:
From $y=(x-(-3))^2$, the vertex is $(-3,0)$ and the axis is $x=-3$.
$$\begin{align*}(x+3)^2&=0\\x&=-3\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=3^2=9$. Draw an upward-opening parabola touching the x-axis at $(-3,0)$ and passing through $(0,9)$.

spec.description: Upward parabola tangent to the x-axis at its vertex.

answer.short: Upward-opening parabola. Vertex $(1,-4)$; axis $x=1$; intercepts $(-1,0)$, $(3,0)$ and $(0,-3)$.
answer.worked:
The vertex is $(1,-4)$ and the axis is $x=1$.
$$\begin{align*}(x-1)^2-4&=0\\(x-1)^2&=4\\x-1&=\pm2\\x&=-1\text{ or }3\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=1-4=-3$. Plot the vertex and intercepts and draw an upward-opening parabola symmetric about $x=1$.

spec.description: Vertex-form parabola with exact intercept labels and symmetry axis.

answer.short: Upward-opening parabola. Vertex and y-intercept $(0,-2)$; axis $x=0$; x-intercepts $(-\sqrt2,0)$ and $(\sqrt2,0)$.
answer.worked:
The vertex is $(0,-2)$ and the axis is $x=0$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2-2&=0\\x^2&=2\\x&=\pm\sqrt2\end{align*}$$
The y-intercept is $(0,-2)$. Plot these features and draw an upward-opening parabola symmetric about the y-axis.

spec.description: Upward parabola with irrational x-intercepts and symmetry axis coinciding with y-axis.

answer.short: Upward-opening parabola. Vertex $(3,2)$; axis $x=3$; y-intercept $(0,11)$; no x-intercepts.
answer.worked:
The vertex is $(3,2)$ and the axis is $x=3$.
At $x=0$, $y=9+2=11$.
Since $(x-3)^2\ge0$, $y\ge2$, so there are no x-intercepts. Draw an upward-opening parabola through $(0,11)$ with minimum point $(3,2)$.

spec.description: Parabola wholly above the x-axis with its minimum and y-intercept labelled.

answer.short: Downward-opening parabola. Vertex $(-1,2)$; axis $x=-1$; x-intercepts $(-1-\sqrt2,0)$ and $(-1+\sqrt2,0)$; y-intercept $(0,1)$.
answer.worked:
Write $y=-(x+1)^2+2$. The vertex is $(-1,2)$ and the axis is $x=-1$.
$$\begin{align*}2-(x+1)^2&=0\\(x+1)^2&=2\\x+1&=\pm\sqrt2\\x&=-1\pm\sqrt2\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=1$. Plot the vertex and intercepts and draw a downward-opening parabola symmetric about $x=-1$.

spec.description: Downward parabola with exact radical intercepts, vertex and dashed symmetry axis.

answer.short:
Upward-opening parabola. Vertex $(-\frac52,-\frac{37}{4})$; axis $x=-\frac52$; x-intercepts $(\frac{-5-\sqrt{37}}2,0)$ and $(\frac{-5+\sqrt{37}}2,0)$; y-intercept $(0,-3)$.

Complete the square to locate the vertex and find the exact roots.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2+5x+\frac{25}{4}-\frac{25}{4}-3\\y&=\left(x+\frac52\right)^2-\frac{37}{4}\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-\frac52,-\frac{37}{4})$ and the axis is $x=-\frac52$.
For the x-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}\left(x+\frac52\right)^2-\frac{37}{4}&=0\\\left(x+\frac52\right)^2&=\frac{37}{4}\\x+\frac52&=\pm\frac{\sqrt{37}}2\\x&=\frac{-5\pm\sqrt{37}}2\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=-3$. Plot these features and draw an upward-opening parabola.

spec.description: Exact radical intercepts, vertex and symmetry axis; enlarged for fractional labels.

answer.short: Downward-opening parabola. Vertex $(-\frac{11}{12},\frac{361}{24})$; axis $x=-\frac{11}{12}$; intercepts $(-\frac52,0)$, $(\frac23,0)$ and $(0,10)$.
answer.worked:
At $x=0$, $y=10$.
$$\begin{align*}10-6x^2-11x&=0\\-(3x-2)(2x+5)&=0\\x&=\frac23\text{ or }-\frac52\end{align*}$$
The symmetry axis lies halfway between the x-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-\frac52+\frac23}{2}\\x&=-\frac{11}{12}\end{align*}$$
Substitute this value:
$$\begin{align*}y&=10-6\left(-\frac{11}{12}\right)^2-11\left(-\frac{11}{12}\right)\\y&=10-\frac{121}{24}+\frac{121}{12}\\y&=\frac{361}{24}\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-\frac{11}{12},\frac{361}{24})$. Draw a downward-opening parabola through the intercepts.

spec.description: Downward parabola with rational intercepts and exact fractional maximum.

answer.short:
Upward-opening parabola. Vertex $(-\frac78,\frac{47}{16})$; axis $x=-\frac78$; y-intercept $(0,6)$; no x-intercepts.

Its minimum value is $\frac{47}{16}>0$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=4\left(x^2+\frac74x\right)+6\\y&=4\left[\left(x+\frac78\right)^2-\frac{49}{64}\right]+6\\y&=4\left(x+\frac78\right)^2+\frac{47}{16}\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-\frac78,\frac{47}{16})$ and the axis is $x=-\frac78$. At $x=0$, $y=6$.
Since $4(x+\frac78)^2\ge0$, the minimum value of $y$ is $\frac{47}{16}>0$. There are no x-intercepts. Draw an upward-opening parabola with these features.

spec.description: Upward parabola entirely above the x-axis, with exact minimum and symmetry axis.

answer.short:
Upward-opening parabola. Vertex $(\frac14,-\frac{57}{8})$; axis $x=\frac14$; x-intercepts $(\frac{1-\sqrt{57}}4,0)$ and $(\frac{1+\sqrt{57}}4,0)$; y-intercept $(0,-7)$.

Complete the square to locate the vertex and find the exact roots.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=2\left(x^2-\frac12x\right)-7\\y&=2\left[\left(x-\frac14\right)^2-\frac1{16}\right]-7\\y&=2\left(x-\frac14\right)^2-\frac{57}{8}\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(\frac14,-\frac{57}{8})$ and the axis is $x=\frac14$.
For the x-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}2\left(x-\frac14\right)^2-\frac{57}{8}&=0\\\left(x-\frac14\right)^2&=\frac{57}{16}\\x-\frac14&=\pm\frac{\sqrt{57}}4\\x&=\frac{1\pm\sqrt{57}}4\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=-7$. Plot these features and draw an upward-opening parabola.
